deferred_source_units.reason: The Ammonite war and three years of specified tribute remain without a demonstrated match. I read 26:1-10 as context: its Minaean gifts to Uzziah are not silently made the same people, king, or payment.

I read the named killer and three named royal victims within the preceding invasion and following captivity. No distinct personal identity match was demonstrated; a general battle comparison would not establish these identities.

The early rising and gathering of city rulers introduce the restoration sacrifice. I read that entire sequence; this transition alone has no sufficiently specific independently supported match in this pass.

The six hundred consecrated calves and three thousand sheep are preserved exactly. The surrounding offerings do not justify assigning this unit an unstated ritual class or matching its totals to a different ceremony.

The third-to-seventh-month accumulation of heaps is read in its full contribution context. No precise matching timetable was established, and an inferred harvest or festival calendar receives no credit.

The named subordinate supervisors are read with the overseers and distribution arrangements. Their specific personal identities have no verified match here; no generic administrative comparison is counted.
The three-years-and-up enrollment wording is read alongside the following priestly and Levitical enrollments. It is not equated with the distinct twenty-year service threshold in 31:17.

semantic_observations: Distinct rulers, occasions, figures, and named people are not collapsed into identities.
The Jericho mercy comparison with Luke is explicitly thematic and claims neither identical events nor explicit quotation.
Same-chapter connections explicitly identify meaningful warning/response, decision/reason, and question/answer or distribution-agent relationships.
The source's 300,000 captives, rooftops, mother names, returned Samaria captives, sanctuary exclusion, and Solomon festival duration are preserved rather than replaced with conventional wording.
Priestly, Levitical, and sacrificial comparisons distinguish different roles, animals, and festivals; no restoration ceremony is identified as the annual Day of Atonement or a Jubilee.
